column2: : With a relaxed fist, gently tap the thigh, front and sides.
: With your fingertips, rub the whole scalp as if shampooing, from the forehead toward the nape.
: Rub your palms briskly together, then stroke the face, the back of the neck and the arms (not the front or side of the neck).
: Rub the scalp with your fingertips, then press the top of the head and the temples.
: Rub the scalp and gently press the top of the head and the temples.
: Gently rub the trapezius muscles with your palms, from the nape toward the shoulder.
: Knead the calf between your palms, without pressing directly behind the knee.
: Knead the muscles on the shoulders (trapezius), without moving up onto the side of the neck, then from the back toward the hips, on both sides.
: Knead the muscle on top of the shoulders with both hands, then with the thumbs along the shoulder blades.
: Gently knead the forearm muscles between the thumb and the other fingers.
: Gently knead the muscle on top of the shoulders (trapezius), alternating hands, without pressing on the side of the neck.
: Very light taps with a cupped palm, only on the muscles between the spine and the shoulder blade, not on the spine, shoulder blade, ribs or below the last ribs (kidneys), then slow stroking.
: Massage each toe: rotate it gently, without pulling hard, then press on the top of the foot in the hollow where the bones of toes 1 and 2 meet (LR3) and in the space between toes 2 and 3 (ST44).
: Massage the sole with the thumb and press on the top of the foot, in the hollow where the bones of toes 1 and 2 meet.
: Massage the ears with quick movements, rolling the lobes and the rim of the outer ear.
: Massage the ears, from the lobes toward the top, gently rolling them between your fingers.
: Massage the ears: gently stretch the lobes, then roll the rim of the outer ear between your fingers.
: Move the ball to the middle of the buttock, slightly to the side, and stay leaning on it, breathing deeply; at tingling or pain running down the leg, take the weight off immediately.
: Stroke the abdomen with your palms, then stay 2 minutes with your hands on your belly, breathing slowly.
: With one palm, stroke the opposite shoulder, from the neck toward the arm, 4–5 times on each side.
: Stroke the lower back and hips with your palms, from top to bottom, 6–8 times.
: Stroke the forehead from the middle toward the temples, then cover the eyes with your palms, without pressure, for 3 breaths.
: Slowly stroke the legs, from the ankles toward the thighs, then stay still with your hands on the abdomen.
: Stroke in long strokes from the ankle toward the hip; raise the leg for 2–3 minutes on a support, relaxed.
: Stroke the nape and shoulders and breathe slowly 3 times.
: Stroke the foot from the toes toward the ankle and repeat with the other foot.
: Stroke the lower back with your palms, with slow breaths.
: Stroke in a clockwise circle around the navel, with very light pressure.
: On the outer side of the lower leg, gently press with the thumb the point in front of and below the head of the fibula (not on the rounded bone, a nerve passes there), holding and breathing slowly.
: Grip the wrist like a pincer: thumb on the palm side (PC6) and index finger on the back of the forearm (TE5), with light to medium pressure; stop at tingling.
: Place both palms on the hips, with the thumbs to the side of the lower spine, and gently press with the palms, simultaneously, on the lateral muscles.
: Repeat on the other side: ball next to the spine, then sacrum, then buttock.
: Breathe slowly and stroke the arms, shoulders and face, as a warm-up.
: Breathe slowly: 4 seconds inhale through the nose, 6 seconds exhale; gently stroke the arms and face.
: Gently raise the shoulders while the recipient inhales and let them drop on the exhale, 5 times.
: Stand or sit and press with the thumb below the knee, to the side of the tibia, and on the inner forearm, at the wrist.
: Stand and, with the ball against the wall, or stay seated and, with your palms, massage the lower back, beside the spine, above the pelvic bones and below the level of the last ribs.
: Rotate the pelvis in wide, slow circles, 5 times in each direction.
: Roll the sole over a small ball, with light weight, for 30–40 seconds.
: Shake out the hands in a relaxed way, then stroke each hand from the fingers toward the elbow, with cream, and breathe slowly.
: Rest the head in your hands and press upward with the thumbs, under the edge of the occipital bone, on the right and left simultaneously, without pressing on the side of the neck.
: Cradle the nape in your hands and slowly press upward with the thumbs under the skull.
: Cradle the nape in your hands and press upward under the skull, then knead the shoulders.
: Cradle the nape in your hands and press upward with the thumbs, under the edge of the skull, on both sides at once.
: Cradle the nape in your hands and press upward, under the skull, on both sides.
: Finish with slow stroking from the nape to the shoulders and down the arms.
: Finish with long stroking, from the nape to the pelvis, and leave 1 minute of quiet.
: Slowly tilt the head toward each shoulder, only as far as comfortable, without pulling it with your hand, then roll the shoulders backward 5 times; stop at dizziness or tingling in the arm.
: Gently stretch the toes toward you, then flex the foot, 5 times.
: Gently stretch the wrist up and down, helping with the other hand, 15 seconds each.
: Stretch the arms above the head, then let them drop; stroke the arms and chest and inhale deeply 3 times.
: Lie on your back, hands on the abdomen, breathe slowly and gently stroke the body.
: Seated, massage the sole with the thumb, then press on the inner ankle, 45 seconds for each foot.

You will need:
Build a weekly plan of sessions. You can see what you have today and export the plan to your calendar (.ics file) for reminders.
Choose another session or ask your doctor.
Choose a quiet, warm room (about 22–24 °C), with a stable, comfortable position supported by pillows.
Choose a side-lying position, with pillows between the knees; avoid lying on your back for long, especially late in pregnancy.
Choose a simple, unscented oil or lotion, such as plain food-grade vegetable oil (for example olive or sunflower; almond oil only if you are not allergic to nuts) or unscented lotion.
Choose the area, then how it feels. You get suitable gentle routines and the warning signs. This is not a diagnosis.
An alternative for large areas, when the fingers get tired; it gives broad pressure that is less pinpoint.

Glide with the whole relaxed palm on the skin, in a long, slow movement, usually from the extremity toward the trunk. The hand stays soft and molds to the shape; the rhythm is steady, like calm breathing. A thin layer of oil or lotion helps the glide.
